module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 680

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/680](https://www.erdosproblems.com/680)
-/

@[expose] public section


namespace Erdos680

open Real

/--
Is it true that, for all sufficiently large $n$, there exists some $k$ such that
$$
p(n+k)>k^2+1,
$$
where $p(m)$ denotes the least prime factor of $m$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_680.parts.i :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in .atTop, ∃ k ≠ 0, (n + k).minFac > k^2 + 1 := by
  sorry

/--
Can one prove this is false if we replace $k^2+1$ by $e^{(1+\epsilon)\sqrt{k}}+C_\epsilon$, for all
$\epsilon>0$, where $C_\epsilon>0$ is some constant?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_680.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∃ C > 0,
    ¬ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∃ k ≠ 0,
    Nat.minFac (n + k) > exp ((1 + ε) * √k) + C := by
  sorry

end Erdos680

review.notes: Both declarations faithfully express the two questions in the copied cited-page text. Part (ii) correctly allows C to depend on ε, but not on n or k, and negates eventual existence rather than asserting eventual nonexistence. Lean experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verified the explicit quantifier expansions, the least-prime-factor semantics, and boundary cases. Eventually n+k ≥ 2 for every permitted k, so minFac's exceptional values at 0 and 1 are harmless. The scratch file compiles successfully. Available status metadata still lists problem 680 as open. Direct access to erdosproblems.com was Cloudflare-blocked; the comparison therefore used its scraped question and remarks, corroborated by Erdős's original paper. The remarks suggest an alternative exponential coefficient but retain the question formalized here.
